budget_items.topic: Recommendation card format: funding sources and rough cost magnitude
budget_items.what_was_said: The consultant proposed that each master-plan recommendation note its funding sources and a rough order-of-magnitude cost (small vs. large) alongside a short/medium/long time frame. The committee discussed adding a simple cost-tier legend so readers can gauge scale.
Members discussed indexing recommendations with dollar-sign symbols to signal rough cost, giving examples of small, medium and large project sizes.
A member noted the town had applied for a competitive state IT grant due earlier in the year and hoped it would be offered again next year to fund technology upgrades.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park and municipal building articles
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said two capital articles -- Marshall Park improvements and a municipal building project -- failed at town meeting this year, attributing it largely to cost concerns and competition with school budget pressures.

decisions.decision: Hold the next committee meeting on the fourth Wednesday of August to review which committees have responded to the feedback request and assign follow-up on the select board, planning board and school committee as priority laggards.
Hold a public information/input session in October, before the town-meeting presentation, to gather citizen feedback on the draft plan.
Move the committee's own working meeting to October 8th and hold the public info session on October 22nd.
The committee chair, not multiple members, will be the one to present the draft plan at town meeting, with consultant support on slides.
Chair will contact the town manager and Tim Murphy about scheduling the draft plan presentation at the fall special town meeting.

minutes.headline: Committee sets fall timeline: Oct 1 committee feedback, Oct 22 public forum, plan to Nov town meeting
minutes.summary: The Master Plan Steering Committee reviewed a proposed report structure and the plan's eight community goals with its consultant, discussed how to format and prioritize roughly 100 recommendations, and spent significant time on implementation strategy, town technology/digitization needs, and getting the town's other boards to submit feedback by October 1. No funding was voted; the committee set a schedule of an October public information session, a November town-meeting presentation of the draft plan, and a subsequent Planning Board vote, and approved several sets of past meeting minutes.

what_happened.line: Committee set a fall schedule: an Oct. 22 public forum ahead of presenting the draft master plan at a November special town meeting.
The committee chair alone will present the draft plan at town meeting, not multiple members, with consultant help on slides.
No funding was voted; the committee discussed adding a cost-tier legend to flag rough scale on roughly 100 draft recommendations.
The committee plans to press other town boards for feedback by Oct. 1, flagging the select board, planning board and school committee as priority laggards.
Members said a Marshall Park improvements article and a municipal building project both failed at town meeting this year, citing cost concerns.

why_it_matters: Residents get one scheduled chance, the Oct. 22 forum, to weigh in before the master plan goes to a town-meeting presentation and a later Planning Board vote.
The roughly 100 recommendations touch town technology, permitting and records systems, but none carries a funding vote yet -- only a proposed cost-tier label.
Two capital articles already failed at town meeting this year, a sign of the competition the plan's own recommendations may face for funding.
